QUOTE: `#ifndef MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS #define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) private_##member #else #define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) member`; "By default a member such as `ssl->state` is declared as `private_state`. Application code that writes `ssl->state` fails to compile"; "Every library translation unit sees real member names. `common.h` is internal and not installed under `include/`, so this does not leak to applications."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer shows both macro branches and explains that code defining the opt-out sees real member names, while ordinary application consumers see `private_` names.
